panels.title: Why the estimate looks low: prompt caching

options.content:
## Why the estimate looks low: prompt caching

Most input tokens here are **prompt-cache reads**, billed at roughly **10% of the base input price** — which is why the estimate sits far below the *Est. Cost Without Caching* figure above.

On **every step** of an agentic session the CLI re-sends the same large prefix, and the model provider serves it from cache instead of reprocessing it. That prefix has three parts:

1. **System prompt** — the CLI's instructions plus your custom `AGENTS.md` / repo guidance.
2. **Tool definitions** — the JSON schema for every available tool (large).
3. **Conversation history** — all prior messages and tool results so far.

`inputTokens` counts the **whole** prefix every turn; `cacheReadTokens` / `cacheWriteTokens` are the cached subset of it.

### Worked example — a large Terraform + AWS repo

You're working in a big Terraform codebase that manages AWS infrastructure, with the **Terraform MCP server** (registry / module / provider tools), the **AWS MCP server** (dozens of AWS API tools), and local **`gh`** calls through the built-in bash tool. Those two MCP servers alone register **dozens of tool definitions** — easily tens of thousands of tokens of JSON schema — and that block is byte-for-byte identical on every request. Together with the system prompt it forms one big **static prefix**.

Now you ask: *"add a VPC module and open a PR."* Copilot runs a loop:

- **Turn 1** — reads `main.tf` and calls a Terraform MCP tool to check the registry. The static prefix (system + all tool defs) is new, so it is **written to cache** once (~1.25× base). The model's reply and the file contents are appended to history.
- **Turn 2** — calls an AWS MCP tool to inspect existing subnets. The *entire* prefix from Turn 1 is unchanged, so it is a **cache read** (~0.1× base); only the new tool result is fresh, full-price input.
- **Turn 3+** — runs `gh pr create`, edits files, re-plans. Each step **re-reads an ever-larger cached prefix** and adds only a little fresh input.

After ~50 turns the model has *read* that growing prefix 50 times but *processed* it fresh only once. `input_tokens` looks huge, yet 90%+ of it is `cache_read_tokens` at a tenth of the price — so the real cost is a fraction of the list-price-without-caching number. The static, identical tool definitions from the Terraform and AWS MCP servers are exactly the kind of large repeated prefix caching is designed to make cheap.

**Rates:** cache reads ≈ 0.1× base input · cache writes ≈ 1.25× base input · fresh input at full rate.

Refs: [OpenAI prompt caching](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/prompt-caching) · [Anthropic prompt caching](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching) · [details](https://github.com/andybaran/copilot-grafana/blob/main/docs/ai-credits.md#how-prompt-caching-affects-the-estimate)

panels.title: Est. Cost Without Caching (USD)
panels.description: Counterfactual: every prompt token billed at the full base input rate (no cache discount). The gap vs. Estimated Cost is what prompt caching saves.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(sc.est_usd_uncached),0) AS "USD" FROM session_credits sc JOIN sessions s USING(session_id) WHERE s.complete AND $__timeFilter(s.start_time) AND s.project IN (${project:sqlstring})

panels.title: Cache Savings
panels.description: Percent of gross list-price cost avoided by prompt caching = (cost without caching − estimated cost) / cost without caching.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round((100.0*(SUM(sc.est_usd_uncached)-SUM(sc.est_usd))/NULLIF(SUM(sc.est_usd_uncached),0))::numeric,1) AS "Saved %" FROM session_credits sc JOIN sessions s USING(session_id) WHERE s.complete AND $__timeFilter(s.start_time) AND s.project IN (${project:sqlstring})

SELECT mc.model AS "Model", SUM(mc.credits) AS "Credits" FROM session_model_credits mc JOIN sessions s USING(session_id) WHERE s.complete AND mc.priced AND $__timeFilter(s.start_time) AND s.project IN (${project:sqlstring}) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

SELECT s.project AS "Project", SUM(sc.est_credits) AS "Credits" FROM session_credits sc JOIN sessions s USING(session_id) WHERE s.complete AND $__timeFilter(s.start_time) AND s.project IN (${project:sqlstring}) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

SELECT date_trunc('day', s.start_time) AS time, s.project AS metric, SUM(sc.est_credits) AS value FROM session_credits sc JOIN sessions s USING(session_id) WHERE s.complete AND $__timeFilter(s.start_time) AND s.project IN (${project:sqlstring}) GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1

SELECT sc.session_id AS "Session", s.project AS "Project", round(sc.est_credits::numeric) AS "Credits", round(sc.est_usd::numeric,2) AS "USD", sc.complete_pricing AS "Complete Pricing" FROM session_credits sc JOIN sessions s USING(session_id) WHERE s.complete AND $__timeFilter(s.start_time) AND s.project IN (${project:sqlstring}) ORDER BY sc.est_credits DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 25

SELECT mc.model AS "Model", COUNT(DISTINCT mc.session_id) AS "Sessions", SUM(mc.input_tokens) AS "Input Tokens", SUM(mc.output_tokens) AS "Output Tokens", round(SUM(mc.credits)::numeric,1) AS "Credits", round(SUM(mc.usd)::numeric,2) AS "USD" FROM session_model_credits mc JOIN sessions s USING(session_id) WHERE s.complete AND $__timeFilter(s.start_time) AND s.project IN (${project:sqlstring}) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY "Credits" DESC NULLS LAST

SELECT display_name AS "Model", vendor AS "Vendor", input_per_mtok AS "Input $/M", cached_input_per_mtok AS "Cached $/M", cache_write_per_mtok AS "Cache-write $/M", output_per_mtok AS "Output $/M", pricing_confidence AS "Confidence" FROM model_pricing ORDER BY vendor, display_name
